headline: Southborough boards advanced key Town Meeting warrant articles, including municipal and school budgets, major capital borrowing, and an appointed Town Clerk proposal.
synopsis: Ahead of the April 11 Annual Town Meeting, town boards focused on warrant preparations and fiscal planning. The Select Board tentatively endorsed a 4.88 percent municipal operating budget increase and voted to support changing the Town Clerk from an elected to an appointed position. The Southborough School Committee held a public hearing on its 3.99 percent budget increase and approved bid specifications for the Neary School feasibility study. Officials across committees also reviewed major borrowing proposals, including an $8.8 million Trottier Middle School roof replacement and a potential multi-year road bond.

highlights.title: Select Board backs appointed Town Clerk proposal
highlights.why: The Select Board voted 5-0 to support Article 25 on the Town Meeting warrant, proposing to make the Town Clerk an appointed role rather than an elected one. If approved by Town Meeting voters, the charter change will require approval on the annual town election ballot.

highlights.title: Select Board endorses FY27 town operating budget
highlights.why: The board voted 3-1-1 to tentatively support the FY27 operating budget, which represents a 4.88 percent increase over the previous year while leaving a $414,000 positive levy balance. A final vote will take place prior to printing the Town Meeting warrant.

highlights.title: School Committee approves Neary feasibility study bid document
highlights.why: Following Special Town Meeting funding approval, the committee voted 4-0 to approve the Request for Services to hire an architectural consultant for Neary Elementary School. The study will evaluate a full renovation as well as deferred maintenance options capped at $15 million.

highlights.title: Trottier Middle School roof replacement project review
highlights.why: Administrators updated the School Committee on plans to replace Trottier Middle School's leaking 1998 roof, estimated at $8,833,964 with an anticipated $3,446,336 state grant. The project goes before voters for a two-thirds vote at Town Meeting and a subsequent ballot vote in May.

highlights.title: Review of multi-year road bond and site remediation
highlights.why: Capital planners and town officials reviewed proposed borrowing articles for Town Meeting, including a $25 million authorization for roads and sidewalks to be drawn down over multiple years and an estimated $900,000 borrowing article for Atwood site cleanup.

highlights.title: Hearing opens on Southville Road MBTA overlay apartments
highlights.why: The Conservation Commission began reviewing a Notice of Intent for two apartment buildings and a clubhouse on a 4-acre parcel at 0 Southville Road. The hearing drew neighbor concerns regarding wetlands and access, and commissioners continued the matter to allow on-site inspections once snow melts.
